The file is called Rift.otf and the family it belongs to is 'Rift',
but the cut inside it is Rift Bold Italic — italic angle -10, the
italic bits set in both head.macStyle and OS/2.fsSelection, and
'Rift-BoldItalic' as its PostScript name. Asking for 'Rift' alone
would let any other cut of the family that happens to be installed
answer, and a title laid out against a Regular's metrics is a title
laid out wrong. So the full name is what gets declared, the same way
It is registered at style normal on purpose. The slant is drawn into
the letterforms; declaring the face italic as well would leave the
canvas — which asks for normal — either missing it or being handed a
synthetic oblique of something else. Normal means 'this file, as
drawn', which is what the two Laugh Society packs are set in.
_comment_css: Not declared in styles.css: this face arrived with a channel and is
registered from this JSON, which is the route content/README.md
describes. Nothing has to be added to the stylesheet for it.
_comment_local: What the machine may already know the face by, tried after the file.
The first is the Windows full name (name ID 4) and is also what the
installer registers the face under; the second is the PostScript
name. Both belong to this file rather than to the family at large, so
a machine answering to either is answering with this cut — which is
exactly what the fallback route is for.
